findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on I/O failure (missing file, permission denied, etc.)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path crashes the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, std::io::Error> and propagate with ? or map_err

findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV line crashes the program instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: return Result and use ? on parse, or map_err to a domain ParseError

findings.problem: Lossy as cast from u32 to u16 (parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16) silently truncates values > 65535
findings.failure_mode: values in range 65536..=u32::MAX silently wrap to 0..65535, corrupting data without any error
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap_or_else(...)) or parse directly into u16 via a checked approach, returning an error on out-of-range

findings.problem: Uses split(',').map().collect() to build a full Vec<String> when only two fields are needed; should use split_once
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation per line, and the Vec is later accessed with unchecked indexing
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',') to get (name, value_str) directly, then trim and parse each

findings.problem: parts[0] — unchecked indexing into Vec<String> with no bounds check
findings.failure_mode: empty lines or lines with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields cause a panic
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and match the Option<(&&str, &str)> result; return error on None

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is I/O (logging) inside the data-parsing core pipeline
findings.failure_mode: side-effectful code is mixed into the pure calculation layer, breaking functional core / imperative shell separation and making the core untestable in isolation
findings.fix: move println! to the imperative shell; the core parsing function should return pure data with no I/O

findings.problem: load_sessions combines I/O (fs::read_to_string) with pure parsing in a single public function
findings.failure_mode: the functional core cannot be tested without the imperative shell; no separation of concerns
findings.fix: split into: (1) a pure fn parse_sessions(lines: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> for the core, and (2) a shell fn load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, SessionError> that reads the file and delegates to the pure core

findings.problem: Record has no type-level invariants; name is a plain String (no uniqueness/non-empty check), value is u16 (allows 0 and any value with no domain constraint)
findings.failure_mode: invalid Record instances (empty name, out-of-range value) can be constructed directly
findings.fix: use a newtype with a fallible constructor that validates invariants, e.g. pub struct Record { name: NonEmptyString, value: ValidatedValue }

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_sessions throughput or allocation behavior
no profiler data for hot path (split, collect, parse) per-line cost
no allocation analysis — Vec<String> collect per line is unbounded
no second-ring test for malformed CSV inputs (missing fields, non-numeric value, empty lines, lines with extra commas)
no command evidence for cargo fmt, cargo clippy, or cargo test
residual_risk: static review only; no commands run. The crate has 8 BLOCKER-class violations spanning forbidden constructs (unwrap, as cast), unchecked indexing, mixed I/O in the pure core, and missing domain invariants. All must be fixed before delivery.
